key_insight: This withdrawn study reported that machine learning could predict distant melanoma metastasis at diagnosis; it did not investigate cancer drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The proposed use was to inform research on staging-imaging selection, not to establish a validated clinical decision tool.
method: Analyzed routinely recorded clinicopathologic and demographic variables from SEER.
Evaluated machine learning models, including an Explainable Boosting Machine.
Examined predictor contributions, decision curves, and imaging costs.
evidence_signal: Among 51,285 adults in SEER (2010–2022), the abstract reported AUROC 0.947, AUPRC 0.610, and specificity 0.843 at 90% sensitivity, with consistent cross-validation performance.
watch_item: The paper is withdrawn, and the abstract reports no independent external validation; its findings and online calculator should not guide patient care.
paper_title: WITHDRAWN: Predicting Distant Melanoma Metastasis at Diagnosis Using Machine Learning
